nodes.text: Well done, son. I can't understand why I never noticed how well you concentrate before!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I could take a wild guess...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Anyway, let's eat!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Awesome. I can't believe how much Emily's father's into me now that I'm a basketball star!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, okay! I'll help you!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Did I seriously just boss you around?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No... Well... Kind of.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Where's your backbone?! Look, I need you to pretend that you're my boyfriend, but that isn't going to work if you don't have a spine, Owen!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I have a spine! Relax.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: No, I'll relax when I'm convinced that you understand how this works.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: We're supposed to be pretending that we love each other, and that means that we `act` like we hate each other.
nodes.text_bbcode: We're supposed to be pretending that we love each other, and that means that we [color=#3b78e2][i]act[/i][/color] like we hate each other.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: So you don't just `agree` to do what I ask you. Got it?
nodes.text_bbcode: So you don't just [color=#3b78e2][i]agree[/i][/color] to do what I ask you. Got it?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, it won't require very much acting.
There's an awkward silence between them.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Not because I'm in love with you! Because you're annoying!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: OooooOOOOooo! You `looooove` me!
nodes.text_bbcode: OooooOOOOooo! You [color=#3b78e2][i]looooove[/i][/color] me!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh great...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hmmm... I don't know.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What?!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You just said I look sloppy. Besides, do rich people like you really need help from poor people like me? Isn't it the other way around?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Are you asking me for money?! I'm not going to `pay you` for friendship, Owen! That's really low, even for you!
nodes.text_bbcode: Are you asking me for money?! I'm not going to [color=#3b78e2][i]pay you[/i][/color] for friendship, Owen! That's really low, even for you!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Who said anything about money? Or is that all you think about from your ivory tower?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Whatever! Fine! I don't need you!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh... Then I guess I'll just be on my way.
Owen starts to walk away!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Wait! Seriously, you cannot leave me here!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm pretty sure I can!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What do I have to do to get you to stay?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hmmm... How about you... Say something nice about me?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: That's it? You can have whatever you want, and your request is a compliment? You must `really` be lonely.
nodes.text_bbcode: That's it? You can have whatever you want, and your request is a compliment? You must [color=#3b78e2][i]really[/i][/color] be lonely.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh, and every insult means you owe me `another` compliment. That's two.
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, and every insult means you owe me [color=#e23b3b][i]another[/i][/color] compliment. That's two.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Okay, fine. I'll get this out of the way quick since it's like impossible to say anything nice about you.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Three.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Grrr!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Okay, fine! You're tall in a way that is appealing. You're nice... Most of the time. And you're... Um, ugh.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You kiss in a way that is not as gross as I expected. I mean, I didn't throw up in my mouth or anything.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Now will you help me?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I guess that's as close to nice as I can expect. Fine. I'll help.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Thanks, Owen.
Paige leads Owen back into the house.

nodes.speaker: Voice
nodes.text: Paige, dear! This century! Tad has a polo match in the evening that he cannot budge!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Uh, excuse us!
Paige grabs Owen, yanks him away from the table, and pulls him back outside!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: I suppose that makes sense.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It does?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Obviously... She gets her eye for fashion from her mother!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: You flirty kook! I wonder if it was one of my fashion ideas that got you this boy, Paige!
Paige speaks under her breath.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Thanks. My mother ate that one up.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Care to tell me what the tofurkey is going on here?

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Ha! That can't be it.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Why not?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Don't get your mother wrong, dear. It's just that you don't possess a `classic beauty.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Don't get your mother wrong, dear. It's just that you don't possess a [color=#e23b3b][i]classic beauty.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: There's no doubt that the half of you that came from me is flawless.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: But your father's genes... What lunacy ever possessed me to accept that man's proposal?
Margot and Tad share a laugh. Paige speaks to Owen under her breath.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Great call. I love being called ugly by my mother!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: How was I supposed to know she'd actually be meaner than you?!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I didn't hear about any parties being thrown today. On Thanksgiving? That's really weird.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, it is really weird. Especially if you didn't hear anything about it.
Suddenly, the door swings open, and Paige is standing there, glaring at Owen!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What are you doing?! You're late, `and` you're underdressed!
nodes.text_bbcode: What are you doing?! You're late, [color=#3b78e2][i]and[/i][/color] you're underdressed!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Who is that? Is that Paige?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Hold on one second.

nodes.speaker: Voice
nodes.text: Paige, dear, is that your boyfriend at the door? Don't let him dawdle! The food is growing cold, and you know how I hate cold lamb!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Who is that? Did she just call me your boyfriend?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: What?! Did Paige just say you're her boyfriend?!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: That's not what she said!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: What's going on?
Paige reaches out and grabs Owen!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just shut up and get in here!
Owen shouts into his phone...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'll tell you later!
He barely has time to hang up on $ZOE before he finds himself at an ornate dining room table setting, standing across from an older couple.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So... I'm the `fourth` one at the party?
nodes.text_bbcode: So... I'm the [color=#e23b3b][i]fourth[/i][/color] one at the party?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ahem. Owen, this is my mother, Margot, and her boyfriend, Tad.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Mother, Tad, this is my... My... Ugh. This is harder to say than I thought it would be!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: This is my `boyfriend,` Owen!
nodes.text_bbcode: This is my [color=#3b78e2][i]boyfriend,[/i][/color] Owen!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Ha! It's no wonder you can't say the word!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: It isn't?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: No. From what your mother tells me, you've never had much luck with boys!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: It's true. She spends far too much time on makeup and very little effort on things that matter... Like accessories.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Grr!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Your mother's jewels are what attracted me to her in the first place. Men are no better than fish. If it's shiny we move towards it.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Oh, I love it when you talk like that. You're so old and wise!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I can accessorize just fine, mother. And besides, not all boys are attracted to shiny things.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: No? I suppose some might not be... So tell us, Owen. What attracted you to my daughter in the first place?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... You want to know about Paige's attractiveness?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: There are so many things to say! And so many of them are amusing!
Paige stares wide-eyed at Owen, her eyes pleading...
Owen sighs.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: But, obviously, I was attracted by her charming personali--
Paige gives Owen a sharp kick under the table!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No! Not that! Something else!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Are you okay?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yup! Forgive me. What I meant to say was, I was attracted to Paige's...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Oh, why are you going into Paige's house?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: For the party? Paige is throwing a big Thanksgiving party. Everyone's invited.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Except for Spencer... And apparently, you.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: A party? Like a family party?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No, like a party thrown by one of our classmates.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Into what?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Paige's house.
All the pieces Ben slices off the turkey are very fatty!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... There's still a lot of meat left on the turkey.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's okay! You're probably just too focused on basketball!
Coach Kessler takes the carving knife back.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'll take over.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Where was my head? Not that it matters...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Now that I'm a basketball star, Coach Kessler thinks I'm awesome no matter what I do...
Coach Kessler is about to start carving the turkey when he catches himself.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What am I doing carving the turkey with a focused guy like Ben around?
He hands the carving knife to Ben and steps aside.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Whoa! Quite the honor, sir.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... I guess I just avoid the fatty areas and slice off all the meat!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, I guess you're right.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So, I was coming off a screen that Spencer set, and Erik was able to dish me the ball perfectly.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I caught it, but I knew there was like no time left on the clock!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: How did you know?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I don't know. Just instinct, I guess.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Instinct! Did you hear that, Emily?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I heard it.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I've been trying to hone Emily's instincts in the pool for years!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, anyway, instead of setting my feet, I just quickly turned and threw the ball up. It just happened to go in!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And he's still modest about it! It was a wonderful shot, son. Didn't you think so, Emily?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yup. Quite the shot.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Actually, I did want to talk about this lovely meal you've prepared for us, Mrs. Kessler!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, mom, this is delicious!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Oh, why thank you!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Yeah, thanks for the wonderful job on the meal, dear.
Coach Kessler gives Mrs. Kessler a kiss on the cheek.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I guess we can hear the basketball highlights later...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, sure.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: See you before six tomorrow.
Paige marches off.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: That was strange... I wonder why Paige really wants me at her party!
You are now playing as Ben...
It's Thanksgiving Day!
Inside the Kessler house, Ben and Emily are sitting next to each other, waiting for Emily's parents to come out of the kitchen with the turkey.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It smells good!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I know, I can't wait! I'm so excited that we're finally going to have some time together!
Ben takes Emily's hand...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Me too, Emily. I know basketball's been a wrench in our plans, but there's no more basketball today! Just Ben!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No swimming either! Just Emily!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Heh. Also, I'm hoping your father might ease up on me now that I'm, you know, 'committed to excellence'... Just a little.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: We'll see...
Just then, the kitchen door swings open and Coach Kessler comes out holding a plate with a huge turkey on it!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: There he is! There's the man of the hour! What are you doing sitting way over there?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Anyone who can shoot the lights out like you deserves a spot at the head of the table!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... Okay.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Who are you? And what have you done with my father?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What?
Ben gets up from his seat next to Emily and moves to the spot at the head.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Remind me, son, how many points did you score in that first game against Piedmont High?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Twenty-five. But the other team wasn't very good.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I won't hear it! What a performance! Emily, how come you never told me your boyfriend was so committed to excellence?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I don't know. I guess it slipped my mind.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: When you hit that three-pointer last week against Xavier High, what was going through your mind?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Do you think we could actually get some turkey this Thanksgiving?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Easy, Emily. I'm just trying to understand the mindset of a champion. You should probably hear this too. Listening to Ben could be good for your swimming.
Ben sees the angry look on Emily's face.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, uh... We don't have to talk about the three-pointer. We can talk about something else.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Nonsense. Don't be modest, son. Athletes aren't paid gobs of money for their modesty!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Duh! I'm throwing a party!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Too much caviar?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: No! I just really need certain people to show up, and if they don't, the party will be ruined.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Am I one of those people?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Maybe.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, if it's that important, I'll try extra hard to be there.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Cool.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: And you said it's a pajama party that starts at seven?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What? Owen! That's--
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Heh heh heh.
Paige punches Owen in the arm.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Jerk!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ow! The jokes are not worth the pain!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Uh... Gross. Stop saying that because you're super wrong. I don't like you!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yes, you do!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Even though you think I'm a poor, low-class simpleton...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: { You want to kiss me! {

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Grr!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, I'm sorry, Paige. I'm not that kind of guy. Even if it would release all the tension you're feeling towards--
Paige slaps Owen!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey! What was that for?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: It certainly released some of the tension!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Because it's going to be the best Thanksgiving... No dry turkey, no awful family, just music and shoes!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Shoes?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I'm having some of my attendants buy shoes for me. And yeah, I know this totally fits with me being some shallow, rich girl, but whatever.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I'm willing to be a walking cliche if it means I'm walking in a perfect pair of heels.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm glad you've accepted who you are.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Anyway, it's going to be a big party, so it doesn't `really` matter whether you come or not.
nodes.text_bbcode: Anyway, it's going to be a big party, so it doesn't [color=#3b78e2][i]really[/i][/color] matter whether you come or not.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Okay, you'll come? Or okay, you understand that your presence is totally unimportant?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, I heard you! I'll need to check with my grandma to make sure that she's all right with it.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: So, if you do come, what time do you think you'll show up? The party starts at six.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Probably sometime around then.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I would feel a lot more comfortable if you came a little early... Just so I could brief you about protocol for this kind of party. Most of my guests will be `way` classier than you.
nodes.text_bbcode: I would feel a lot more comfortable if you came a little early... Just so I could brief you about protocol for this kind of party. Most of my guests will be [color=#3b78e2][i]way[/i][/color] classier than you.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So... You want me to be there early?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Yes. What are you going to wear?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Something nice?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ugh. Just make sure whatever shirt you wear has a collar on it.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You mean, like a t-shirt?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What?! You can't be--

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Relax. Relax. I'm just messing with you.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Oh... Well, you can understand why I might take you seriously, considering what you're wearing now.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Did you just tie some blue rags together for pants?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: These are jeans.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Do poor people call rags 'jeans'? That's cute. So I'll see you in a `nice` shirt and `non-rag` pants `before` six?
nodes.text_bbcode: Do poor people call rags 'jeans'? That's cute. So I'll see you in a [color=#3b78e2][i]nice[/i][/color] shirt and [color=#3b78e2][i]non-rag[/i][/color] pants [color=#3b78e2][i]before[/i][/color] six?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Are you okay?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What do you mean?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, you said you don't care if I go, but then you seem really concerned about when I show up and what I wear...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It sounds like...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ew! No!
A moment passes.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Okay, maybe. I mean, since you like me.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I never said I liked you.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well it's super obvious!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Let's check the log, shall we?
Owen pretends to unravel a scroll and reads from it.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: On this day in history, Paige indeed declared that she 'has it crazy bad' for Owen Harris.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Lies! Just come to the party, okay?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Why?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Duh! You don't have anybody to spend Thanksgiving with. Or are you forgetting that your parents are separated?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Thanks for bringing that up! And are you forgetting about Grandma Betty?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Like she counts! She's probably going to bingo night or church or something. You know, some old person gathering.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You're out of touch with reality in so many ways.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Tell me I'm wrong!
Owen glares at Paige for a second.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Okay, fine! She's got a knitting group! But it's not an old person gathering!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ha! You're so cute when you're wrong.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: But she's only going to that `if` I decide not to have dinner with her. Her plan is to eat a Thanksgiving dinner with me.
nodes.text_bbcode: But she's only going to that [color=#e23b3b][i]if[/i][/color] I decide not to have dinner with her. Her plan is to eat a Thanksgiving dinner with me.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well, if you want to have turkey scraps in a shack, I guess that's your right.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It sounds better than eating caviar alone at your mansion!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Sorry, low blow.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Big time...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, I didn't mean it.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You promise?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I promise. Now tell me, why should I go to your party?
He smoothly lays the ball in!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Made it!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Good! That's how a layup should look! Now all of you... Get outta my face and go enjoy your holiday!
The players cheer as they rush off the court and into the locker room.
Later, in the locker room...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Can't wait to stuff a whole pepperoni pizza in my face!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm pretty excited for my grandma's special Thanksgiving pumpkin pie!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Have fun by yourselves, dorks. I'll be spending Thanksgiving `with my girlfriend.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Have fun by yourselves, dorks. I'll be spending Thanksgiving [color=#e23b3b][i]with my girlfriend.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Speaking of ladies, that reminds me of one thing I am crazy thankful for!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What's that?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: My man Owen has cured himself of Paige-itis!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That's true! You haven't been making any absent-minded references to horses, high-fashion, or Paige's goddess-like body!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Nice try. I never said anything about her body...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: ...Did I?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: It doesn't matter. You're your own man again, bro! Ever since you got that sweet pair of shoes like I told you to!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Yeah. You said buy some shoes, so that's what I did. I bought them. Definitely not a gift...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: And the moment you did was the moment you got that diva out of your system.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You know, she's not as bad as you think.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Uh huh. You're too nice, dude. Anyway, see you suckers later.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yeah, happy Thanksgiving, Owen!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You too. Later!
Owen is the last guy out of the locker room. The halls are empty due to the Thanksgiving holiday, except for a few people milling about...
...Including Paige, who is standing at her locker. Owen walks by.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Still here, huh? Forgot what commands to give your limo driver?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Har har. My last class ran late. Are you going to one of those soup kitchen thingies for Thanksgiving?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No. Unfortunately, I don't have much free time for volunteering.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Who said anything about volunteering?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Wow. I walked into that one.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Yeah, you did. Anyway, I'm throwing a huge Thanksgiving party. If you wanna come, I guess you can.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: That's weird of you. Isn't everyone going to be spending time with their families on Thanksgiving?

nodes.text_bbcode: That's it! A promise is a promise! We're going to run [color=#e23b3b][i]all[/i][/color] day!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You're not serious, are you?

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: You bet your butt I am! Now get on that baseline!
Everyone stands on the baseline.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Go! Run! Run!
Twenty minutes later...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Coach. `Huff huff.` We get it. Lesson learned.
nodes.text_bbcode: Coach. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff huff.[/i][/color] We get it. Lesson learned.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Lesson? This isn't a lesson! This is a punishment! Now run!
An hour later!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: I can't feel any of my legs!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'm completely blind in one eye!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: This is so stupid, Coach. Just let us go home!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: I would... But Owen can't make a layup!
The guys groan!
Several hours later...
Grandma Betty shuffles her way into the gym.

nodes.speaker: Grandma Betty
nodes.text: Owie! There you are! I've been worried sick!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Ma'am, this is a closed practice.

nodes.speaker: Grandma Betty
nodes.text: Nonsense, I need to talk to my grandson.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What. `Huff!` What is it. `Huff!` Grandma?
nodes.text_bbcode: What. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] What is it. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] Grandma?

nodes.speaker: Grandma Betty
nodes.text: I just wanted to make sure you're okay, dear?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No. `Huff!` Help. `Huff!` Torture.
nodes.text_bbcode: No. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] Help. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] Torture.

nodes.speaker: Grandma Betty
nodes.text: That's nice, sweetie. I'll be in bed by the time you get home. See you tomorrow.
Grandma Betty slowly shuffles her way out of the gym.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No. `Huff!` Come. `Huff!` Back!
nodes.text_bbcode: No. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] Come. [color=#e23b3b][i]Huff![/i][/color] Back!

nodes.text: But it's too late. As she leaves the gym, Owen knows that they'll be stuck there...
While everyone else eats turkey and stuffing and mashed potatoes and pie...
They'll be running. And it's all his fault.
The ball floats through the air, casually grazing the edge of the net.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ugh...

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: I didn't even know you could airball a layup! Everybody run!
The players all groan as they run toward the far wall and back!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I've only got `one` eye, and I could do this blindfolded!
nodes.text_bbcode: I've only got [color=#e23b3b][i]one[/i][/color] eye, and I could do this blindfolded!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: That doesn't even make sense!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Just make the stupid layup!
Coach hands Owen the ball again.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: All day. I'm `not` kidding.
nodes.text_bbcode: All day. I'm [color=#e23b3b][i]not[/i][/color] kidding.

nodes.text: Owen runs toward the hoop, jumps, raises the ball up for a layup, and...
The ball slams into the bottom of the rim!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oops!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Worse than the last one! Everybody run!
All the players sprint down the court and back.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: It's a layup! How hard is it?!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: As soon as he makes one, you can all go home and enjoy your Thanksgiving holiday.
Owen takes a breath, tries for another layup, and...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I get that you're trying really hard with my dad, and I appreciate that `so` much.
nodes.text_bbcode: I get that you're trying really hard with my dad, and I appreciate that [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] much.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But Ben, you don't have to go this far. He's just going to put more and more pressure on you to win, the same way he does with me.
Emily takes Ben's hand.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: There isn't anything more you have to do to win me over.

nodes.speaker: Voice
nodes.text: Ben! Get in here! I've got some highlights to show you!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I should go.
Ben automatically starts moving towards the house, away from Emily... But she holds onto his hand, pulling him back.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, your dad's calling me.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I know. This is what I've been trying to tell you... You don't have to go to him just because he orders you to.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: He's not ordering me. Don't you understand? I want to spend time with him.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Why?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You just don't understand, do you?
Ben lets go of Emily's hand and walks back into the house.
You are now playing as Owen...
Paige lowers her voice to a whisper.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Look... I think Tad is going to propose to my mother tonight.
Owen sits back down, shocked.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Tad? The guy we've been eating with. The guy with a stick up his--

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Yeah. That guy.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Lame.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: When I found out last week, I just kept thinking about how I'd feel. What it would be like if he proposed. It made me ill.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: And then I imagined hearing my mother say, 'Yes,' as though that guy is actually even half as good as my father is...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I couldn't bear it, Owen. I just couldn't.
Paige's eyes start to well up with tears.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, it's okay. You convinced me. I'm not going anywhere.
Tad returns to the room, followed almost immediately by Paige's mother.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Rosemary is deeply sorry for the meal. I realized that I was probably keeping her from her family, so I gave her the rest of the day off.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: After today's duck l'orange, you probably should have just fired her altogether. What an overcooked mess!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I just hope the day can be salvaged...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Perhaps I can help.
Tad reaches out with a spoon and lightly taps on one of the glasses. He stands.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Oh no...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Margot, I haven't known you nearly as long as I'd like before something like this.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: But we're not getting any younger.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: It is with my gravest sincerity that I inform you of my intention to marry you.
Tad pulls out a velvet box and opens it, revealing a ring with a massive diamond.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: It's so beautiful. Of course I'll marry you!
Paige's mother throws her arms around Tad. Owen looks to Paige and sees that she's crying.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Look how happy my Paige is for us!
Owen leans over and whispers to Paige.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, it'll be okay.
Then he takes her hand underneath the table and holds it in his.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm here for you...
As Tad and her mother laugh delightedly, Paige gives Owen's hand a squeeze.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So then you `don't` care about basketball!
nodes.text_bbcode: So then you [color=#3b78e2][i]don't[/i][/color] care about basketball!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Just because I'd skip my game for you doesn't mean that I don't care about basketball.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It just means that I love you more than some sport.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Aww... Well, that was smooth.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That's why they call me Smooth Butter Ben!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I hope they don't!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Basketball is my new thing, Emily!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It's everything to me!
Emily crosses her arms!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And what am I?! Nothing?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Oh, well, wait... This is a hypothetical, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, and now I'm `hypothetically` mad at you!
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah, and now I'm [color=#3b78e2][i]hypothetically[/i][/color] mad at you!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Are you sure? Because it seems like you're `really` mad at me.
nodes.text_bbcode: Are you sure? Because it seems like you're [color=#e23b3b][i]really[/i][/color] mad at me.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You wouldn't give up a swim meet to come watch me play ball, would you?
Emily uncrosses her arms...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No, I guess not.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Besides, basketball is also my ticket to a good relationship with your dad!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You embarrassed me!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh, well, I'm sorry for `trying` to perpetuate `your` lie!
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, well, I'm sorry for [color=#e23b3b][i]trying[/i][/color] to perpetuate [color=#e23b3b][i]your[/i][/color] lie!

nodes.text: Tad's phone rings, and he rises from the table.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: I simply `must` take this.
nodes.text_bbcode: I simply [color=#e23b3b][i]must[/i][/color] take this.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: And some might consider that rude!
Tad ignores Owen and walks out of the room. Paige smiles at her mother.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Perfect! This would be a great time for you to get to know Owen without any inter--

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: In a minute, dear. I didn't think Rosemary spent very much time on this meal at all.
Paige's mother mutters to herself as she rises.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: What's the point of having a Thanksgiving meal if your servants can't cook it properly?!
She marches off toward the kitchen, leaving Owen and Paige alone...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, I just ran into some unexpected traffic on the way over here.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Inexcusable. I don't understand why you didn't factor in the possibility of traffic.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I was also told that there would be a lot of people--
Paige shoots him a glare.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Er, people who would not be driving their cars.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: An online map. The internet told you, is that it?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: To put it in overly simple terms, yes.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Tsk. Tsk. Another strike against today's generation.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Grrr!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No, I don't think I will.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Well!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Excuse me?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No offense to anyone here, but it seems like you already have some set opinions about people being late.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Why would I just feed you more ammunition?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Ammunition?!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: And while I'm at it, don't `you` think it's rude to call out other people for doing things you think are rude?
nodes.text_bbcode: And while I'm at it, don't [color=#e23b3b][i]you[/i][/color] think it's rude to call out other people for doing things you think are rude?

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Well... Um...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: He kind of has a point, Tad.
A nearby grandfather clock chimes!

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: That reminds me... Owen, I couldn't help but notice you were late arriving.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Punctuality is one of those underrated traits I find so lacking in our youth.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I couldn't agree more.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: I don't know if there's anything ruder. I always make it a point to arrive early to functions.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: One of the many reasons I adore you!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Blech.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Owen, would you care to explain the circumstances of your tardiness?

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Really? Am I that out of the loop? Who's the designer?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Spencer... Kale.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Spencer Kale. I've not heard of him. But this look is atrocious.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: The designer must be new and avant-garde.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, that's right!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I `loathe` avant-garde! It feels like he's saying... 'Poor is now rich.'
nodes.text_bbcode: I [color=#3b78e2][i]loathe[/i][/color] avant-garde! It feels like he's saying... 'Poor is now rich.'

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: What a bothersome idea!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Very bothersome!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Whoops!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I don't get the joke.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It's a commentary on the needs of the upper class to adopt an air of superiority, even regarding things it does not understand.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Oh... I get it.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Aha. I do too now. That `is` rather funny.
nodes.text_bbcode: Aha. I do too now. That [color=#3b78e2][i]is[/i][/color] rather funny.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Yes, it was.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Is...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: Is what?! Spit it out, man!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: High fashion!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I always thought my Paige could be an actress. But her arms are too flabby, don't you think?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Thanks!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Um...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: The point is moot, Margot. I think you're forgetting that acting requires a certain charisma that `few` possess.
nodes.text_bbcode: The point is moot, Margot. I think you're forgetting that acting requires a certain charisma that [color=#e23b3b][i]few[/i][/color] possess.

nodes.text: At `few,` Tad gives Paige a mean glare. A servant interrupts the moment by delivering the next course of the meal, which Owen cannot identify.
nodes.text_bbcode: At [b]few,[/b] Tad gives Paige a mean glare. A servant interrupts the moment by delivering the next course of the meal, which Owen cannot identify.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Looks... Like food!
Owen realizes that he's still wearing his jacket. He takes it off and hangs it on the back of his chair.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Owen, what are you wearing, dear? You did know this was a formal occasion?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I told him.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Whatever. It really puts me into a dismal mood, looking at his attire. I feel like I'm dining with one of the servants!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ahem. Paige did tell me. This outfit is...
Paige groans.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Sports?!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, I play football, and I just started playing basketball.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Throughout history, the elite have always kept commoners entertained with acts of physical barbarity!

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I see times haven't really changed...

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: In this analogy, you're like a lowly gladiator, Owen. A piece of meat.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I get it.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Lovely. Just lovely. Do you have any favorite performances?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... I really loved... Erik Ericson's performance... In... The Passing Drill.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: I've not heard of that one. Is it off-Broadway?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah. It's `very` off-Broadway.
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah. It's [color=#e23b3b][i]very[/i][/color] off-Broadway.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: What? Why are you just sitting there like an invalid!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Sports! I enjoy sports!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Ahem. Who's up for dessert?!
You are now playing as Owen...
Owen is once again sitting at the ornate dining table next to Paige.

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: So Owen, Paige has told us very little about you. She's always been scatterbrained like that. Gets it from her father.

nodes.speaker: Tad
nodes.text: The apple does not fall far from the tree.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What do you mean by that, `Tad?`
nodes.text_bbcode: What do you mean by that, [color=#3b78e2][i]Tad?[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Margot
nodes.text: Never mind. `I` want to know about Owen. Why don't you tell us something about yourself?
nodes.text_bbcode: Never mind. [color=#3b78e2][i]I[/i][/color] want to know about Owen. Why don't you tell us something about yourself?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, okay... Well, I like to play--
Paige kicks Owen underneath the table!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I mean... I `enjoy...`
nodes.text_bbcode: I mean... I [color=#e23b3b][i]enjoy...[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Excuse me?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I love your daughter, and nothing is going to get in the way of that.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Not basketball practice, not swim practice, and not you.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Awww! That was really sweet Ben!
Coach Kessler picks up the carving knife.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh oh.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Watch yourself, young man.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You might have earned some points with me by demonstrating this commitment to the basketball team...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: But all of that can be erased in a heartbeat if you keep acting the way you did just now.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I apologize, sir.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Excuse me?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I never said my goal was to be a champion.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Well then what are you playing for?!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I think you can put hard work into a sport, enjoy it, and get something out of it without adding all the pressures of winning.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I don't understand. Why play if you're not focused on winning?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I think you broke my dad.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: It's nice to hear such a refreshing attitude.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: A weird attitude is what it is!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, uh, winning is nice too.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: There! Much better!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I'm glad you're so willing to change to make my dad happy, Ben.
You are now playing as Ben...
Back at the Kessler house, Ben and the Kesslers are enjoying the turkey that Ben carved.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: I heard there's a big dance coming up! Are you two going?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Unfortunately, no. The dance got scheduled for the same day as our big game in Willow Glen.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And I can't go because it's so far away. The game could run really late.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's right. We have a swim meet the following morning.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Emily and I are so busy now, I decided to make time for her.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: How did you manage that, dear?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I talked it over with my coach, and he says it'd be okay if I missed a practice or two.
Coach Kessler nearly chokes on his food!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You will do no such thing!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I won't?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Dad! You're not his coach!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'm sorry, son, but that's not the thinking of a champion. If you skipped practices just to spend time with my daughter, I'd be `very` disappointed in you.
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm sorry, son, but that's not the thinking of a champion. If you skipped practices just to spend time with my daughter, I'd be [color=#e23b3b][i]very[/i][/color] disappointed in you.

options.label: Then you'll have to be disappointed.
Who said anything about me being a champion?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I just wish I could say the same for Emily...
You are now playing as Owen...
Owen arrives at the massive, ornate front door of Paige's family estate.
He doesn't see any people and can't hear any noise coming from within the house.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, I'm only a little bit late. But where is everyone? I don't want to be the first guy here!
He takes out his phone and calls Spencer.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Owen! Did you see it? I can't believe Surf 'N' Turf Murph broke that katana with his face!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I thought he was a goner when Tres Samurai hypnotized him with their anthem... Sushi Rolls in Mexico City. Have you been watching?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No, I'm at Paige's party. Are you coming?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Uh, I didn't hear anything about a party, dude.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh, sorry. I guess she didn't invite you.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Big surprise.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You don't know anyone going to this thing?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Nope. Just hearing about it now. You know who you should ask? $ZOE.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Somehow I doubt that $ZOE's anywhere near the top of Paige's invite list.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Yeah, but if there's something going on, $ZOE probably knows about it.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Good point... Actually, I could see Paige making a big deal to $ZOE about how she's `not` invited.
nodes.text_bbcode: Good point... Actually, I could see Paige making a big deal to $ZOE about how she's [color=#e23b3b][i]not[/i][/color] invited.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I could see that too... And then $ZOE would get all mad, and say something about how Paige is just jealous because she didn't win Social Chair.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Would she?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Then Paige runs up to $ZOE and starts pulling her hair, and then they fall down in some mud, and then $ZOE puts Paige into a Pretzel Twist Suplex!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Pow! Then--

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey! Spencer! Want to check back into reality?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Whoops. Sorry, bro, my mind's on wrestling! Anyway, commercials over, gotta roll! Call $ZOE!
Spencer hangs up, and Owen calls up $ZOE.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Owen... Hi.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hey, $ZOE! Happy Thanksgiving!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: You too...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Is everything okay?
There's a pause on the line, then...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Yeah, sorry. Everything's fine. What's up?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh, well, I'm just about to go into... Uh... Into...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You've got one second to convince me not to just get up and leave. My grandma's staying up later than her usual bedtime to make a nice meal for me!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just stay, okay?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Why should I? You lied to me, Paige! You used me to try and impress your mom.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Are you that dumb?! You think I had you come here to `impress` my mother?!
nodes.text_bbcode: Are you that dumb?! You think I had you come here to [color=#3b78e2][i]impress[/i][/color] my mother?!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You're like the least impressive guy I know!

Later that day, at Owen's place...
Grandma Betty, Owen, and Paige are sitting around the dinner table, holding hands.
And last, I'm glad to have people in my life whose hands I want to hold.
Couldn't have said it better myself! Let's eat!
As Grandma Betty starts serving up mountains of delicious stuffing, Owen talks quietly to Paige.
You okay?
Am I okay that my mother and Tad ditched us to go out and celebrate their nauseating engagement? No...
But?
But I'm glad you talked me into coming to this shack for turkey scraps.
Good.
Oh and don't stuff yourself with stuffing! I've got a pumpkin pie baking in the oven!
Oh my gosh! This food is amazing!
Kind of reminds you just how much we have to be thankful for.
You mean, like servants?
No, Paige, I meant--
Hee.
I see what you did there.
Gotcha.
And the three of them enjoy their feast for the evening.
And across town...
$ZOE sits down at the table with Sam and Aunt Cathy.
At their feet, Puddles happily drools over a bowl of food...
Woof. Woof.
Turkey anyone?
Yes, please!
Aunt Cathy starts serving portions of turkey and mashed potatoes and hands the plates to the girls.
Yum! I love how Thanksgiving revolves around food... That makes it the best holiday.
Yeah really!
So girls... What are you thankful for this time around?
Well, there have been a lot of sad things that have happened in the past month or so..
Breaking up with Howard... Turning all the school cliques against one another... Cutting the basketball team out of the Snow Ball...
And now, I guess, Owen is going out with Paige...
You don't know that...
I heard what I heard. But it's all these things that make it kind of hard to think about what I'm grateful for...
You have been through a lot.
Well, today is about setting those things aside. I'm still happy that I'm Social Chair...
But more importantly, I'm so grateful to have both of you in my life.
And Sam, what about you?
Well, since I haven't been dumped by a guy who's interested in another girl again, I'd call that a win.
I'm pretty grateful for that.
So there are no new guys in your life?
Good luck with that conversation, Aunt Cathy. I've been trying to find Sam a date for the Snow Ball for a couple weeks now.
Hey, I don't have to worry about things like that. Remember that fortune teller at Paige's Halloween carnival?
She said my love life wouldn't pick up until mid-February. I'm waiting until then.
She said that you'd find love near Valentine's Day? That's a little predictable.
That's fine with me. Why waste time looking now when Mr. Perfect is going to fall right in my lap later?
Well, that makes me sleep easier at night.
The girls laugh, and Puddles wags his tail.
Woof!
Well, girls, raise your mugs...
Sam and $ZOE lift their mugs of apple cider. Aunt Cathy does the same.
I am thankful for this wonderful Thanksgiving to have both of you in my house. Sam, you are my beautiful girl...
Aw, Mom...
And $ZOE, I'm so glad my sister let me keep you for now. I think of you as one of my own.
Aunt Cathy, that's so nice!
Cheers and a happy Thanksgiving!
